 Order

The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail in the event of his arrest by Puttur Town Police Station, D.K. in Cr.No.103/2023 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 504, 507 read with Section 34 of IPC, pending on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and ACJM Puttur.
2. The allegations of the complaint disclose that, the petitioner/accused
being retired
as Assistant Executive Engineer

has availed hand loan of Rs.90 lakhs from the complainant and towards repayment of the said amount, he had issued three cheques amounting to Rs.25,00,000/-,
Rs.15,00,000/- and Rs.50,000/- and the said cheques were presented and bounced.

It is further NC: 2024:KHC:10215 alleged that he has repaid Rs.2,00,000/- on 06.02.2023, Rs.5,00,000/-, on 08.02.2023, Rs.7,50,000/- on 04.03.2023, and Rs.9,00,000/- on 13.03.2023, totally amounting to Rs.33,50,000/- to the complainant.
It is alleged that he did not repay Rs.56,50,000/- and assured him of repayment of the same in few days.
But, later on the complainant demanded to pay back the money.
The petitioner/accused used to slander the complainant in social Media and also called to him from different mobiles and threatened him.
In this regard, a complaint came to be lodged and on the basis of the complaint, FIR came to be registered.
The petitioner apprehending his arrest approached the learned Sessions Judge.
The learned Sessions Judge has rejected anticipatory bail petition filed by the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner is before this Court.
3. Heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader.
Perused the records.

The allegations disclose that in the month of February 2022, the petitioner/accused has availed hand loan of Rs.90 lakhs from the complainant and out of that he repaid Rs.2,00,000/-,
Rs.5,00,000/-, Rs.7,50,000/- and Rs.9,00,000/- and he was due to the tune of Rs.56,50,000/-.

Further allegations disclose that three cheques issued towards repayment of Rs.90,00,000/- were bounced and later on, petitioner used to slander the complainant in social Media and also made Sri Shivamurthy C vs State Of Karnataka on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125605126/
2 calls to him from different mobiles and threatened him.

sentences.text: The allegations of the complaint itself disclose that it is a personal commercial transaction between the parties.
When the cheques were already issued, nothing prevented the complainant from initiating the proceedings under the provisions of Negotiable Instruments Act.
5. Considering the nature of the offence in my considered opinion, there is no impediment for admitting the petitioner on anticipatory bail.
The other apprehensions raised by the learned High Court NC: 2024:KHC:10215 Government Pleader can be meted by imposing certain conditions.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the petition needs to be allowed and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The petition is allowed.

ii) The petitioner is directed to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in the event of his arrest in Crime No.103/2023 of Puttur Town Police Station, D.K. registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 504 and 507 read with Section 34 of IPC, on executing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- with one surety, for the like-sum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer or the concerned trial Court,
subject to following conditions:
a) Petitioner shall surrender himself before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order and in the event of his surrender Investigating Officer/SHO shall release him on bail as directed.
NC: 2024:KHC:10215 b) He shall not directly or indirectly tamper with any of the prosecution witnesses.
c) He shall not indulge in any similar offences.
d) He shall make himself available to the Investigating Officer for interrogation whenever called for during the course of investigation.
e) He shall mark his attendance before the Investigating Officer/SHO between 9.00 a.m. and 5.00 p.m. on every first Monday of the month till the final report is submitted.

Sd/-
